definitions.explanation: A deep, seemingly bottomless body of water or chasm. Used literally for deep waters and figuratively for profound, unknowable, or dangerous depths of the mind, evil, or abstract concepts.

examples.japanese: {深淵|しんえん}を{覗|のぞ}き{込|こ}んだ。
{人間|にんげん}の{心|こころ}の{深淵|しんえん}は{計|はか}り{知|し}れない。
examples.english: The depths of the human heart are unfathomable.

examples.japanese: {深淵|しんえん}を{覗|のぞ}く{者|もの}は、{深淵|しんえん}からも{覗|のぞ}き{返|かえ}されている。
examples.english: He who gazes into the abyss finds the abyss gazing back into him.
examples.notes: A well-known paraphrase of Nietzsche, frequently quoted in Japanese.

notes:
REGISTER:
A literary and formal word. In everyday speech, {底|そこ}なし or simply {深|ふか}い{穴|あな} would be used. {深淵|しんえん} carries a philosophical or dramatic weight and appears frequently in literary, philosophical, and religious contexts.

USAGE:
The Nietzsche quotation {深淵|しんえん}を{覗|のぞ}く{者|もの}は… is widely known in Japanese and has made this word familiar even to non-literary readers.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {深淵|しんえん}を{覗|のぞ}く: to gaze into the abyss
- {深淵|しんえん}に{落|お}ちる: to fall into the abyss
- {心|こころ}の{深淵|しんえん}: the depths of the heart
